findings.current: whose blood will be caught up in that storm
findings.defect: The Korean says the blood will be mixed into the wind, preserving the wind image from the preceding blood-wind metaphor. “Caught up in that storm” replaces that image.
findings.rationale: The source says “그 바람에 섞인 피” (“blood mixed into that wind”), not blood caught up in a storm.
findings.replacement: whose blood will be mixed into that wind

findings.defect: “Forgive me” is added. The Korean self-corrects from an informal to a respectful first-person pronoun before saying he misspoke; the explicit apology comes later.
findings.rationale: The source says “내가, 아니 제가 실언을 했습니다,” which contains the self-correction and admission, but no request for forgiveness.

findings.current: We have the justification and the strength to bring the Emperor down.
findings.defect: The Korean describes both their grounds and their power as strong; the English drops that emphasis.
findings.rationale: “강한 명분과 힘” means strong justification and strength/power, not merely justification and strength.
findings.replacement: We have strong grounds and power to bring the Emperor down.

summary: The translation is faithful overall, with a few minor shifts in imagery and dialogue nuance.
